title: Same sepsis spec, three engines: where compute time goes
interpretation: Wall-clock for one matched 48 h severe-sepsis run of the SAME model specification, executed by three interchangeable engines. BioGears 8.2.0 (the original C++ whole-body physiology engine) takes ~3.38 h; the Tellurium/roadrunner exact-SBML extraction of the same core takes ~2.81 h (BioGears + Tellurium figures are committed meta.wall_s from the engine-runtime data consolidated into this study). Both are dominated by the same cost: integrating the stiff 91-state ODE (a stiff implicit solver, CVODE, is required and already compiled C). A PyTorch neural surrogate of the same core runs the 48 h / 576-step rollout in ~0.2 s — roughly 40,000x faster than the exact SBML path — because it replaces the ODE solve with one forward pass per step. The surrogate trades accuracy for speed (it stays bounded over the horizon but is NOT clinically accurate — in fact degenerate across severity; see study 05), so it is a fast approximate tier, not a drop-in replacement. The point of the figure is the span: the same spec runs across four-plus orders of magnitude of compute by swapping the engine, and the compute in the exact engines is spent almost entirely in stiff ODE integration.
caption: Two views of where the compute goes for the same sepsis spec. Left: full 48 h run wall-clock under BioGears (~3.38 h), Tellurium exact SBML (~2.81 h), and the PyTorch surrogate (~0.2 s) — committed numbers. Right: live per-step cost measured on this machine — one exact CVODE step of the real 91-state model ~526 ms vs one surrogate forward pass ~0.04 ms (exact is ~13,000x; exact values from bench_live.json). Both show the same thing: the exact engines spend their time in the stiff ODE solve; the surrogate replaces it with a forward pass.
provenance: Left panel — BioGears + Tellurium: committed meta.wall_s (severe 48 h) from the engine-runtime runs consolidated into this study; surrogate: ~0.2 s (folded-in surrogate work). Right panel — live per-step benchmark measured by bench_live.py (TelluriumProcess CVODE per interval on sources/biogears_sepsis.ant vs a viva-torch NeuralProcess forward pass), warm, written to bench_live.json (the exact/surrogate per-step numbers quoted in the caption are read from there). Chart script: make_runtime_compare.py.
